I understand the ordered goal as toss/catch, spin/toss/catch twice, spin/hold, preserving the palm-up wrist and finger style while adapting to uncertain placement and ball physics. I will distinguish visible motion from inferred contact and unobservable sphere orientation, declare my verification criteria before simulation, prove and learn contact primitives, and train the final deployable policy with reinforcement learning.

Reconstruction: the ball has a visible seam and logo, but full attitude is not uniformly observable. A local LK/sphere fit finds about 476 degrees of incremental motion over frames 78–151 and 419 over 226–294, with only 79% and 69% accepted increments; these are incomplete estimates, not full spin measurements. The short middle turn (180–198) gives about 69 degrees path and 25 degrees net, 89% accepted. I will inspect and validate local contiguous intervals before using relative rotation as primitive evidence. Ball translation fits 313/315 masks with median analytic replay IoU 0.945; shared gravity-constrained flight fits use a weakly calibrated focal about1546px versus MoGe1300px. Default MANO fit has visible IoU0.725 and 91% contact within10mm but still needs contact-depth and blur-boundary refinement.

At 03:15 UTC the complete contract check is VALID, but I have not yet recorded a frozen version: artifacts are being refined and will be revalidated together before recording. Quality checks distinguish format validity from physical fidelity. The original full-mask circle fit creates false depth jumps when the hand occludes the ball during dips; excluding boundaries within5px of the measured hand mask repairs most of this, but narrow exposed arcs make radius ill-conditioned, so I am adding a weak temporal-radius prior. The complete default-contact refinement quality report has no failed checks (anatomical contact and continuity remain warnings). I will preserve exact snapshots when recording and continue refinement through the full reconstruction hour.

The explicit thumb/opposed-tip term improves the visible grasp but a constant learning rate .02 makes late MANO iterations oscillate, and only103 penetration probes can miss a deep vertex. body.text: All10 quality checks now pass for the version2 snapshot. Remaining image disagreement is primarily joint occlusion: the raw sphere/mask silhouette IoU .935 becomes .881 when fitted MANO is rendered together. The original depth-order loss constrains hand-labelled pixels but does not explicitly keep hand vertices behind ball-labelled pixels. An owned-copy occlusion_order term now penalizes hand vertices lying in front of the rendered front sphere surface where the measured mask says ball. Prediction: actual joint replay ball IoU improves while signed penetration and anatomical grasp remain valid. This is a measured visibility constraint, not a new hand motion.

The extra occlusion-order fit does not yet justify replacing version2: sampled joint replay IoU .8835 is close to baseline, while worst analytical penetration worsens3.44→5.71mm and hand IoU .7236→.7217. I am comparing identical frame subsets and visual sheets before keeping any change. Version2 remains the recorded best, all10 checks pass. An object-only reconstruction contact sweep is also calibrating the looked-up rebound prior; this is physical-property identification, with no robot training scene built during Stage1.

Version2 remains best: the visibility-order trial gains only .0017 sampled ball IoU (.88179→.88351) while worsening penetration3.44→5.71mm and hand IoU .7236→.7217, so it is not kept. For the remaining reconstruction time I am checking held-out hand masks:63frames (frame mod5=2) are withheld from fitting, a new fit starts only from HaWoR rather than the already-fitted reference. This measures fitting robustness to withheld silhouettes; it is not an independent source of ground truth.

Object-only contact identification found why restitution should not be assigned from a damping ratio alone: low damping-ratio solref showed a large time-step dependence. The direct stiffness/damping pair(-100000,-60),1mm felt margin, matches the ITF type2 rebound prior at0.5ms (1.464m) and1ms (1.359m) from2.54m drop, with effective deformation~17mm. This is a prior for ball versus a rigid granite-like surface, not a measured hand contact. I am checking finer time steps and rest stability before updating the reconstruction physical model. Soft hand-cover contact and uncertain ball wear will need separate treatment later.

Held-out-mask check finished:63withheld frames have median IoU .7042 versus .7150 on given masks, from a fit initialized only with HaWoR. The full-mask separated3 hand remains best. Ball contact prior finalized at direct gains(-100000,-58),1mm ball-only margin:2.54m drops rebound1.461/1.456/1.371m at .25/.5/1ms, all within ITF type2 range;17–18mm effective deformation.1ms rest jitter reaches .0138m/s and is explicitly a numerical limitation. This updates only the object reconstruction scene and evidence, not a robot training scene.

Uncertainty audit corrected an overconfident provisional number before the final reconstruction record:12mm described silhouette-fit error conditional on camera, not absolute monocular depth. The current trajectory now propagates focal sigma250px, uniform ITF size prior,3degree gravity direction and2/5pixel contour uncertainty; absolute translation sigma is roughly0.1m, correlated across frames. Absolute ball-attitude validity is explicitly false, while accepted local texture increments remain estimated. This strengthens the limitation statement; flight rise remains much better constrained by the sensitivity profile.

Final three-panel comparison reviewed at0,45,55,67,120,160,170,180,196,210,240,310: wrist dip/launch, open flights, catches and opposing holds agree qualitatively. Hidden finger shape remains approximate, particularly deep dip frames160/196; I will not retarget those joint poses literally. Local roll directions in anatomical-hand axes differ across phases: first mostly palm-normal, short middle mostly finger-longitudinal, final largely thumb-side axis. This matters for later primitive design. All-pass reconstruction checks are consistency evidence, not hidden-pose ground truth.

Exact wrist axes, phases and quantitative evidence are preserved. I will retain this reference and begin criteria/simulation only after04:05:38UTC; no robot training scene exists yet.

Last reconstruction measurements from recorded v3: fitted wrist speed median .054,p95 .501,max1.106m/s; acceleration max15.33m/s². Ball release2.35–2.50m/s therefore involves finger contribution as well as the wrist. Human fitted index/middle/ring PIP flexion decreases roughly17/22/25degrees from initial hold to first flight, with DIP extension too. Later criteria/controller design must preserve finger opening and a moderate down-up wrist pulse, not silently replace it with a much faster wrist-only launch. Exact human angles remain approximate; measurements saved in research/finger_flex_reference.json.

Simulation construction began only after the reconstruction hour and criteria r0020. Initial palm cup is not stable: the ball rolls off laterally under the reference~30degree palm tilt. I am correcting explicit hand–ball material pairs (URDF geoms need names) and using kinematics to choose a genuinely supporting cup. No valid starts, feasibility or policy success is claimed. The shared model keeps the hand mass .7088kg, published PD/impedance controllers and per-tick hardware audit; torsional contact must pass CPU/GPU outcome parity before GPU training is relied on.

The first geometry-only cup IK is rejected: it placed thumb links through index/middle links by up to16mm, causing immediate back-driven joint speed violations and ball ejection. The original guess had no such speed problem but could not support the ball. I have added actual simulated inter-finger collision distances to the IK objective and moved the nominal ball farther toward the finger bowl, so the next candidate must be both nonintersecting and dynamically stable. This is controller/scene development, not a learned-policy result.

Randomized raw insertion exposed a start-model problem: only14/32hold starts passed and6had hardware violations; many otherwise-held balls rotated23–48degrees while settling, with4drops. A ball cannot appear interpenetrating rigid finger geometry. I am testing a physically explicit user-placement setup: slowly lower the externally supported ball into the selected cup, let the compliant fingers equilibrate, then release with no object forcing during the episode. Every placement failure and setup hardware count is retained; no seeds are discarded. This represents the stated human placement, and the independent hold start check still judges the released state. If drops remain I will change the hand pose, not shrink the placement range.

Slow user placement eliminates setup hardware violations but the released hold still fails21/32starts: restoring the pre-placement nominal joint targets releases stored finger deflection and rotates the ball. I am testing a hold policy that latches the actually loaded initial encoder pose, which is available at deployment, rather than immediately pulling back to the unloaded pose. The chosen unloaded starting pose stays fixed; the loaded joint state varies physically with ball placement. This does not change the gate thresholds or discard any placement. If it is stable, both loaded-pose spread and placement coverage will be reported explicitly.

Latching loaded joints prevents all32hardware violations but only12/32start checks pass; residual ball motion is mostly settling rotation, with no drops. The start rule requires an already-resting supported ball, so I am making the simulated human setup finish that physical settling before the episode: keep the chosen unloaded hand target fixed, gradually remove human support, then let the ball rest with no object force. Every seed remains in the test, including any setup drop. I also choose a shallower12degree palm tilt, within the predeclared style range and30degree reference tolerance. Actual post-placement state spread, setup transients and original placement coverage will be reported, not confused with raw insertion states.

A setup-loop bookkeeping bug left the nominal1.2s hold test at only.12s (2tick commands were not restored to20ticks after settling). I corrected it before any suite registration. The sampled resting states looked supported, but the short test was not a valid start-check result. The rerun restores the50Hz policy step and uses a slower gradual removal of human support, with setup and episode hardware counts reported separately.

The corrected slow-setup hold check passes31/32released starts with32/32episode hardware-safe; one seed continues settling, and2setup trials briefly exceed a joint speed. I am increasing setup translational damping and allowing3s unforced settling, without changing the chosen hand targets or filtering seeds. A visual-only white seam proxy is being added in Blender so rollout videos expose ball rotation; it has no collision or mass and does not imply recovered branding/absolute video attitude.
